scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

F-01.statement: Dispute tickets (n=2440) have median response time 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA.

F-02.statement: Of billing-db disputed bills, 1240 have read_type ESTIMATED and 1785 have read_type ACTUAL (3025 total).

F-04.statement: billing-db tariff_change_log returned 0 records, indicating no tariff rate changes were logged for the period examined.

F-05.statement: Field route completion for manual-read accounts in 2026-08..09 was 0.88 against a 0.95 target, covering 9200 manual-read accounts.

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2 states the utility may request route priority changes, executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

F-07.statement: billing-db accounts_estimated_last_cycle returned 320 accounts with estimated bills last cycle, spanning 40 distinct routes; only account_id and route fields are present.

F-08.statement: route-log lagging_routes returned 14 records with distinct completion and route values; sample record shows completion 0.70 for route R-00.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING.statement: Dispute ticket volume is driven mainly by slow/inadequate ticket handling, so an AI agent that auto-answers tickets and auto-corrects bills will bring volume back to baseline.

H-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules around August altered how reads/estimates are accepted, causing a wave of incorrect bills.

H-AMI-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: AMI register read delivery from the vendor (ORG-AMI) via the nightly MDMS export degraded or became invalid starting in August, forcing estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-HANDOFF-FAILURE.statement: Manual meter read uploads from the contracted field service (ORG-FIELD) via the daily upload handoff became incomplete or invalid starting in August, increasing reliance on estimated bills.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: Field staffing shortages at ORG-FIELD caused missed read routes, driving the increase in estimated/incorrect bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Across 2440 tickets, response times (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days) are within the 3.0-day SLA, so the dispute surge is not explained by slow or inadequate ticket handling. This undermines the response-speed framing used to justify the AI auto-answer agent and points toward an upstream cause (billing/read quality).

Disputed bills split 1240 ESTIMATED vs 1785 ACTUAL (3025 total), so the larger share of disputes sits on bills built from ACTUAL reads, not estimate-substituted ones. This weakens explanations that rest solely on estimate substitution from upstream AMI/field read failures and points toward a billing-side issue (e.g. import/validation/tariff) touching both read types.

Monthly dispute counts run ~600/month in June-July 2026 (610, 590) then roughly double to 1180 in August and 1260 in September. This confirms the magnitude and timing of the surge referenced in the initial request, but the data itself says nothing about its cause.

The billing-db tariff_change_log query returned zero records, meaning no tariff rate changes were logged. This rules out a tariff change as a cause of the disputed bills, but says nothing about the separate billing import validation rule log (DA-RULES) referenced by H-RULE-CHANGE, which remains untested.

Field route-log data for 2026-08..09 shows manual meter-read route completion at 0.88 against a 0.95 target across 9200 manual-read accounts, a real but modest shortfall and no prior-period baseline for comparison. This gives a concrete, measurable gap in field read coverage but, taken with E-02 (majority of disputed bills are ACTUAL read type, not ESTIMATED), it cannot by itself explain most of the dispute surge.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead), a non-authoritative source, claims no tariff change occurred this year, which agrees with the already-recorded authoritative E-04 finding (billing-db tariff_change_log: 0 records). The claim corroborates but adds no new decision-relevant information beyond E-04, since E-04 is already AUTHORITATIVE and COMPLETE on this question.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (non-authoritative) claims ORG-FIELD has been short three meter readers since July, causing routes to run late and those customers to receive estimated bills. This supports a staffing-driven mechanism for the field hypotheses but does not address why most disputed bills (E-02) are ACTUAL-type rather than ESTIMATED, and SH-FIELD has a disclosed incentive to attribute problems to staffing (contract headcount increase).

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 authoritatively confirms that route priority changes may only be requested by the utility and are executed only after Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) confirmation. This corroborates the existing K-DISPATCH human-approval constraint on push_route_update rather than introducing a new rule.

E-09.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: The billing-db accounts_estimated_last_cycle query (E-09) returned a narrower result than the work item anticipated: 320 distinct accounts had estimated bills last cycle, spread across 40 distinct routes, but only account_id and route fields are present (no read_type, tariff, or import-status data). This gives a route-level denominator for currently-estimated accounts that could be cross-referenced with the pending route-log lagging_routes query to help quantify the field-staffing share of the surge (U-FIELD-CONTRIBUTION-SIZE), but by itself confirms or denies no root-cause hypothesis.

E-10.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log lagging_routes (E-10) returns route-level completion for 14 specific routes (sample: R-00 at 0.70), giving granularity beneath the 0.88 aggregate completion rate already recorded in E-05. It identifies which routes are behind target but does not itself quantify how much of the dispute surge those lagging routes explain.

U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION.question: Did the billing import validation rule change log (DA-RULES / billing-config) actually record a change around August, and what specifically changed?
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION.decision_impact: Confirms or refutes the core causal premise (H-RULE-CHANGE); without it, remediation design and root-cause sign-off cannot proceed.
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION.resolution_path: Query billing-config's rule-change log for the Aug 2026 window and cross-reference entries against the E-02/E-03 timing before remediation design proceeds.
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION.safe_placeholder: Treat the rule-change mechanism as unconfirmed; do not finalize remediation scope until DA-RULES is reviewed, per SC-ROOT-CAUSE-CONFIRMED.

U-AMI-READ-QUALITY.question: Is AMI register read delivery/validity from MDMS actually fine during Aug-Sep, given mdms-export is currently DEGRADED with a HOLD on ACCESS_PENDING (recovery_decision seq 73) and no fallback?
U-AMI-READ-QUALITY.decision_impact: If AMI read quality degraded, it could independently contribute to incorrect bills alongside or instead of the rule change, changing remediation scope.
U-AMI-READ-QUALITY.resolution_path: Escalate to ORG-AMI (vendor) for provisioned mdms-export access to resolve the ACCESS_PENDING hold; re-run read-event checks once access is granted.
U-AMI-READ-QUALITY.safe_placeholder: Treat AMI read-event findings as unverified and exclude them from root-cause confirmation until mdms-export access is restored; do not block other investigation actions on this tool.

U-FIELD-CONTRIBUTION-SIZE.question: What share of the dispute surge is attributable to field staffing-driven estimate substitution versus the billing-rule mechanism?
U-FIELD-CONTRIBUTION-SIZE.decision_impact: Affects how much remediation effort/priority goes to field staffing/route fixes versus billing-rule fixes.
U-FIELD-CONTRIBUTION-SIZE.resolution_path: Segment disputed bills by read type and route-completion status to quantify the staffing-attributable share once DA-RULES is reviewed.
U-FIELD-CONTRIBUTION-SIZE.safe_placeholder: Treat staffing contribution as secondary/unquantified; do not size route-fix remediation until segmentation analysis completes.

U-AI-AGENT-FIT.question: Even once root cause(s) are confirmed, is an AI agent that auto-answers tickets and attempts automated fixes an appropriate/safe response given K-BILLWRITE prohibits automated bill writes?
U-AI-AGENT-FIT.decision_impact: Determines whether any automated-fix capability can be built at all, or whether the solution must stay diagnostic plus human-executed remediation.
U-AI-AGENT-FIT.resolution_path: After root cause confirmation, review K-BILLWRITE and K-DISPATCH with SH-BILL and SH-FIELD to scope which response/remediation steps may be automated versus must stay human-executed.
U-AI-AGENT-FIT.safe_placeholder: Ship only diagnostic/investigation actions and human-reviewed draft responses; exclude any automated bill-write capability (write_bill_adjustment is out of scope per SC-BILL-ADJUSTMENT-OUT-OF-SCOPE).

U-SUCCESS-METRIC-GAMING.question: Could 'dispute volume back to baseline' be satisfied by suppressing/auto-closing tickets (SH-CS has an incentive to lower ticket backlog) rather than fixing underlying bill accuracy?
U-SUCCESS-METRIC-GAMING.decision_impact: Determines whether dispute-volume recovery alone is a trustworthy success signal or must be paired with an independent accuracy metric.
U-SUCCESS-METRIC-GAMING.resolution_path: Pair SC-DISPUTE-VOLUME-RECOVERS with the independent SC-BILLING-ERROR-RATE-TRACKED metric so volume drops are cross-checked against real accuracy gains.
U-SUCCESS-METRIC-GAMING.safe_placeholder: Do not accept dispute-volume decline alone as success; require the billing-error-rate metric to also improve before declaring the surge resolved.

U-FIELD-BILL-HANDOFF.question: Is the H-FIELD-BILL daily-upload handoff (manual meter reads, ORG-FIELD to ORG-UTIL) actually delivered completely and semantically valid, given its delivery_status and semantic_validity are both UNKNOWN?
U-FIELD-BILL-HANDOFF.decision_impact: If this handoff is failing, field-read-derived bill/dispute counts used in the investigation could be unreliable, affecting the staffing-contribution analysis.
U-FIELD-BILL-HANDOFF.resolution_path: Check ORG-FIELD daily-upload logs/receipts against billing-db and route-log to confirm delivery completeness and semantic validity of H-FIELD-BILL.
U-FIELD-BILL-HANDOFF.safe_placeholder: Treat field-read-derived counts as provisional; do not use them alone to size remediation until handoff validity is confirmed.

U-MDMS-BILL-HANDOFF.question: Is the H-MDMS-BILL nightly-export handoff (AMI register reads, ORG-AMI to ORG-UTIL) actually delivered completely and semantically valid, given its delivery_status and semantic_validity are both UNKNOWN and mdms-export is DEGRADED?
U-MDMS-BILL-HANDOFF.decision_impact: If this handoff is failing independently of the billing-import rule, it could be a contributing or alternative cause requiring separate remediation.
U-MDMS-BILL-HANDOFF.resolution_path: Once vendor-provisioned mdms-export access resolves the ACCESS_PENDING hold, verify H-MDMS-BILL delivery completeness and semantic validity against MDMS source logs.
U-MDMS-BILL-HANDOFF.safe_placeholder: Treat AMI-derived bill data as unverified pending handoff validity confirmation; do not rely on it to rule out AMI-side contribution to the surge.

problem_definition.requested_solution: SH-CS (requester) wants an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills (CL-01).
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-03).
Majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025) are ACTUAL read type rather than ESTIMATED (1240) (E-02).
Ticket response times remain within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d SLA) despite the surge (E-01), ruling out slow handling as the cause.
Field manual-read route completion is below target (0.88 vs 0.95) across 9200 accounts, Aug-Sep (E-05).
problem_definition.root_problem: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-03), and the majority of disputed bills are built from ACTUAL meter reads rather than ESTIMATED (1785 vs 1240 of 3025, E-02), while no tariff change occurred (E-04). Current evidence best supports that a change to billing import/validation rules around August altered how both ACTUAL and ESTIMATED reads are accepted during the billing-import step, producing a wave of incorrect bills that drove the dispute surge, with field staffing shortages (E-05, E-07) contributing a secondary, smaller share limited to estimate-substituted accounts.

details.requested_solution: SH-CS (requester) wants an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills (CL-01).

structural_remedies.rationale: Read-only authoritative query on an existing tool surface (billing-config), no approval or protected action required; 225 minutes remain.; residual gap: This is diagnostic, not corrective; the actual rule-change content and its causal link to the ACTUAL vs ESTIMATED split (E-02) remain unknown until the query runs.

structural_remedies.description: Once the specific rule change is identified via R-CONFIRM-RULE-CHANGE, have Billing Operations (SH-BILL/ORG-UTIL) revert or correct the billing import/validation rule in billing-config, a process/config fix.
structural_remedies.rationale: No listed constraint blocks a config-rule correction (K-BILLWRITE only governs writes to individual customer bills, not import rule config); contingent only on completing R-CONFIRM-RULE-CHANGE first.; residual gap: Already-issued incorrect bills still require manual, Billing-Ops-approved correction per K-BILLWRITE (no automated bill writes); exact share of surge attributable to the rule vs staffing (U-FIELD-CONTRIBUTION-SIZE) stays open.

structural_remedies.description: Address the secondary field staffing/route-completion shortfall (E-05, E-07) through the existing contract/approval channel: SH-FIELD proposes route/staffing adjustments, executed only after Field Operations Manager runtime confirmation per K-DISPATCH.
structural_remedies.rationale: Any push_route_update must go through K-DISPATCH's mandatory runtime confirmation, which is structurally feasible, but closing a staffing gap (hiring/contract headcount) cannot be completed within the remaining ~225 contest minutes.; residual gap: Only addresses the smaller ESTIMATED-bill subset (A-STAFFING-IS-SECONDARY-ONLY); SH-FIELD's self-reported shortage (E-07) is non-authoritative and incentive-biased (A-SH-FIELD-CLAIM-RELIABILITY), so magnitude is unverified.

structural_remedies.description: Escalate to the AMI vendor (ORG-AMI) to resolve the mdms-export DEGRADED/ACCESS_PENDING state so MDMS read-event logs (DA-MDMS) can actually be queried to test AMI read quality (U-AMI-READ-QUALITY).
structural_remedies.rationale: Acquisition explicitly requires vendor provisioning of export access; no indication this can be granted within the remaining contest window.; residual gap: H-AMI-DELIVERY-FAILURE stays REJECTED on existing E-02 evidence, but U-AMI-READ-QUALITY and the H-MDMS-BILL handoff (delivery_status/semantic_validity UNKNOWN) remain unverified regardless.

structural_remedies.description: Have ORG-UTIL run a one-off manual check of H-FIELD-BILL and H-MDMS-BILL handoff logs (delivery_status, semantic_validity) rather than building full monitoring instrumentation, to reduce the A-DATA-COMPLETENESS-UNKNOWN assumption.
